context: A teacher walks a uni student through a global-affairs paper
purpose: Teach: 麻痺/朝鮮半島/自律/均衡/過度/引っ張っ/木材/機内

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 論文、朝鮮半島の物流麻痺と東アジア均衡の話、面白い切り口ですね。
lines.en: Your paper — logistics paralysis on the Korean Peninsula and East Asian balance — that's a really interesting angle.
lines.style: Warm, focused attention. Leans forward slightly on the dash. Clear-eyed recognition of genuine thought. Pace measured but not slow. The tone of someone who reads a lot of papers and noticed this one.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。木材輸入の停滞と、機内貨物の代替について書きます。
lines.en: Yes. I'm covering stagnant timber imports and air-cargo alternatives.
lines.style: Steady, slightly formal. Small breath before the list. Precise — not rushed, but economical. The careful tone of someone stating their thesis clearly, half to her, half to himself.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 過度な依存を引っ張ってきた構造、自律的に組み替える話も入れて。
lines.en: And make sure you pull in the structural dependencies — the whole piece about how systems autonomously restructure themselves.
lines.style: Conversational but authoritative. Gesture on 'pull in.' Not lecturing — offering the next level up. Warm underneath the directness. The voice of someone who wants to see him go further.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 政策の自律性、章を割いて論じます。
lines.en: I'll dedicate a whole chapter to policy autonomy.
lines.style: Quick nod in his voice. Small conviction underneath — he's already thought about this. Quiet certainty. Not defensive, just confirming he's already heading that way.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 地域間均衡の数値、出典は丁寧に。
lines.en: And for those regional-balance numbers, make sure your citations are solid.
lines.style: Practical, almost matter-of-fact. Slight pause before 'solid' — the weight of experience. Not worried about him, just looking out. The tone of someone who has seen good papers sink on soft sourcing.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.style: Quiet assurance. Slightly warmer than before — he's taken something in. Short exhale. The kind of acknowledgment that means 'I hear you and I'll do it.'
